System Requirements Definition, Process for Generating System Requirements, p. 558

The System Requirement Definition activities begin with the transformation of the integrated set of needs into a set of requirements for the SoI. These requirements must be appropriate to the level that the SoI exists within the system architecture and communicate "what" the SoI must do to meet the needs, avoiding requirements that state implementation of "how" to achieve the design realization of the physical SoI.

The record has one probe, one run and one evidence, which hides a distinction Z draws: a probe is an individual prompt-response pair; a run is a sequence of prompt-response pairs forming a trajectory within a session; sessions are stateful and LLM-system behaviour is highly context sensitive, nonlinear in the sense that a small change in input can cause large changes in output, especially when trajectories are continued. Test plans are not limited to single probes: they support strategies that determine probes according to a state feedback policy (semantic state feedback). Shapes M2-Wire (per wire: from an output port on a part to an input port on a part, one item kind, ends typed by the seam) and M2-Part (per kind of part: every input present on exactly one wire, every output going somewhere) replace the port-targeted shape; M4-ProcessDag checks the succession graph has no cycle (loops stay admissible by ruling if the end state needs them; none does). queries/wiring.rq explains every port locally and renders as a table on the assemblage page. SCI-11 restated.

Every wiring must be checkable and explainable locally. At the part level, all of a part's input ports and output ports are examined to ensure that every input is present and every output goes somewhere. At the wire level, each wire is examined for where it comes from and where it goes: an output port on a part to an input port on a part. If all rules are defined over kinds of parts and kinds of ports, then enforcing the rules for all parts and wires yields a well-constructed wiring diagram; ports are how wires are addressed. This is essentially the typed block diagram once directionality and the cardinality rules are enforced: one input wire per port, and output wires that may split as long as they are informational.

In all likelihood the EPO is a process DAG. Loops are allowed if they are needed to guarantee that the final output record has full requirements traceability in both directions and test coverage, computable by SHACL constraints.

The ability to ensure a full record with executable checks on traceability and coverage is precisely what allows the final result to be trusted, and it supports drilling in and deterministically answering the "why" questions related to that result.

Ruling R-16: ISO 9000:2026 deprecates this word as a synonym of conformity; this specification reclaims it on purpose, and says so, not as a synonym but for a special case: the correctly constructed record, whose conformance is fulfilment of the EPO's record-keeping requirements and so a conformity in its own right. Two reasons. It separates fulfilling a requirement of the system (conformity, attested by a person) from satisfying the record-keeping requirements of the EPO (conformance, checked by machine). And it avoids SHACL's own word for the check, validation, which by this specification's split is verification.

The record is correctly constructed: it satisfies every rule the Evaluation Process Ontology's shapes state about how an evaluation must be recorded. A mechanical yes or no, produced by machine. If the record conforms, the process was followed, its data is shaped, its required fields are filled, and coverage can be computed. A special case of conformity: fulfilment of the record-keeping requirements.
earl:outcome earl:passed on an attestation: the system fulfilled the criterion

Ruling R-16: conformity is fulfilment of a requirement (ISO 9000:2026). Its deprecated synonym conformance is reclaimed, deliberately, for the special case of a record correctly constructed to the EPO's shapes.

Fulfilment of a requirement, in the ISO sense: the system under test conforms to an acceptance criterion when its response fulfils it, as a named person attests. For the machine-checked shape of the record itself, see conformance.
the scope of the specification; no node of its own
Zargham and Hollek, for this specification (ruling R-47, sheet 06-10)

The evaluation of a deployed AI system against the needs of a specific domain and deployment context, judged by people who know that domain. The class of evaluation this specification is for; OG-CAIE is the way it is performed here.
sysml item def ServiceAgreement; epo:ServiceAgreement, signed by the sponsor and the authorized representative
Ruling R-27 closed concern C-24: the 2026 wording (3.3.13) is the 2015 wording (3.4.7), captured as screenshot 38. Ruling R-21 calls the agreement a contract to perform the OG-CAIE as a service.

The binding agreement between the sponsor organization and the testing organization to perform OG-CAIE as a service. It is signed by the sponsor and by the testing organization's authorized representative, precedes the requirement set and follows the mission, the need and the proposal in the record.
epo:CustomerRole, the genus of epo:EvaluationCustomerRole and epo:TestItemCustomerRole; sysml part def Organization

Ruling R-21 named the sponsor organization the customer; the tbox audit (sheet 08, on Z's instruction) keeps customer as ISO 9000's genus and makes its two specializations explicit as narrower terms: evaluation customer (the sponsor) and test item customer.

A person or organization that receives a product or a service. Two products change hands around an OG-CAIE evaluation, so there are two customers: the evaluation customer, the sponsor, receives the evaluation as a service; the test item customer receives the AI system under test, as the sponsor sometimes does and as the affected populations do when they use it. The two may be the same organization, and the record says whether they are.
epo:weight; sysml attribute weight on AcceptanceCriterion

The weight each acceptance criterion carries, set by the consequence of the system getting it wrong in this deployment. Coverage is computed against these weights so it reflects consequence rather than count.
epo:Determination, an earl:Assertion and prov:Activity; earl:outcome passed, failed or cantTell; sysml item def Determination

The ruling, made on one or more evidence items, that a criterion's expected result was met, was not met, or cannot be told. It is the ruling made on evidence, recorded with an EARL outcome of passed, failed or cannot tell, made by machine or by a named person, and it is what an attestation aggregates for a criterion.
epo:Trajectory holds the dialogue as ordered turns
The ordered prompts to, and responses by, the system under test within one session. Its recorded form is the trajectory.
epo:DsoRelease (version, approvedBy); sysml item def DsoRelease
Zargham and Hollek, for this specification (ruling R-47, sheet 06-10)

The vocabulary and relations of the problem domain, imported from an existing ontology or supplied by domain experts, that equip one evaluation with the concepts it needs. A domain expert supplies or approves the release used. It changes when the domain changes.
sysml part def OgCaieEvaluation; action def EvaluationProcess

Systematically determining how far something meets its specified criteria. An OG-CAIE evaluation determines, for a declared requirement set, which criteria the system under test met, and reports coverage and performance separately.

epo:EvaluationCustomerRole; epo:sponsorRole on the service agreement, the statement of work, the delivery and the acceptance; epo:actsOnBehalfOf the affected populations; sysml part def SponsorOrganization

Tbox audit (sheet 08, on Z's instruction): the customer of the evaluation service, distinguished explicitly from the customer of the AI system under test. Ruling R-21 introduced the party under the headword customer. When the sponsor is not the test item provider, its position is that of a second party in ISO/IEC 17000's sense.

The organization that receives the evaluation as a service: the sponsor. It states its mission and its need, agrees the requirement set with the testing organization under a contract, decides the statement of work, and receives and accepts the report and the recommendation. It may also be the test item customer, and it may commission the evaluation on behalf of affected populations who are, or who are affected by, the test item's customers.
sysml part def EvaluationOperator; epo:evaluationOperatorRole; prov:Person

Ruling R-23: the operator and the domain expert are abstract actor categories in distinct EPO slots; the system operated is the evaluation, not the test item. Replaces the label AI evaluation expert of ruling R-10, kept as an altLabel.

The technical expert who operates the evaluation: declares the requirement set with the sponsor, writes the test plan, administers the probes to the test item, collects the responses and the evidence per the plan, and drafts the report and the recommendation. The operator makes determinations but does not attest; attestation belongs to the domain expert. An abstract actor category, filled by a named person in each evaluation.
Zargham and Hollek, for this specification (ruling R-47, sheet 06-10)

Rulings R-31 and R-32: the steps are not invented. Each step in vocabulary/epo.ttl cites the process step it matches: the contracting lifecycle (need, propose, agree, access, deliver, accept) matches the ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 agreement processes, ISO/IEC 17000 access, scheme and acceptance, ISO 9000 contract and the 29119-2 test environment and completion report; scope and declare requirements match the ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 acquisition, stakeholder needs definition and system requirements definition processes as SEBoK describes them; plan, execute and report match the ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-2 test strategy and planning, test execution and test completion processes as SEVOCAB defines them; determine and attest matches ISO/IEC 17000's review, decision and attestation. The EPO operationalizes those steps as executable checks.

The reusable, domain-independent description of how a rigorous evaluation is run: the standard operating procedure whose six steps, performed inside the contracting lifecycle, make a coverage claim checkable when followed. It assumes a Domain-Specific Ontology is in place and does not change across domains.

Ruling R-17. Downward: requirement to acceptance criteria to test plan to probes (shapes S2, S3). Upward: attestation to evidence to turn to probe to criterion to requirement (shapes S6, S8; queries/traceback.rq). Coverage: the weighted share of criteria with an attested outcome (shape S7; queries/coverage.rq).

The record of one evaluation, bound by the Evaluation Process Ontology: the DSO release, the requirement set, the test plan, the probes, the sessions and their trajectories, the evidence, the attestations, the report and the recommendations, with who did what and when. The EPO determines what must be present for requirements traceability in both directions and for coverage, and makes all three checkable by machine; a conformant record therefore provides both traceability directions and coverage.
epo:EvaluationServiceProviderRole; epo:testingOrganizationRole on the service agreement; sysml part def TestingOrganization

Tbox audit (sheet 08, on Z's instruction): the provider of the evaluation service, distinguished explicitly from the provider of the AI system under test. Ruling R-21 introduced the party under the headword provider.

The organization that provides the evaluation as a service: the testing organization. Its authorized representative signs the contract and delivers the report, its evaluation team does the work, and its machines keep the record. When it is independent of the test item provider and has no user interest in the test item, its activity is third-party in ISO/IEC 17000's sense; the record states that independence as a fact.
sysml part def EvaluationTeam inside TestingOrganization

Ruling R-28 (concern C-31): anchored to the SQuaRE evaluator, the same family as the adopted term evaluation (ISO/IEC 25001), with ISO 9000:2026 audit team and SEVOCAB assessment team as the two neighbours. ISO 9000:2026 3.12.1 defines an audit as a systematic and independent process for obtaining evidence and evaluating it objectively, with no legal bearing; the connotation is the reader's, and it is avoided. Rulings R-10 and R-21: the technical experts are members, not support.

The evaluators within the testing organization who jointly perform one evaluation: at least one domain expert and at least one evaluation operator, each an evaluator in the SQuaRE sense, the person who performs an evaluation. What ISO 9000 calls an audit team is the same shape of thing for an audit; the word audit is kept out of the headword because readers hear legal bearing in it that neither standard intends.
epo:expectedResult on AcceptanceCriterion; sysml attribute expectedResultStated

What the system under test should observably do if it meets an acceptance criterion under the probe's conditions. Stated on the criterion before testing, so the criterion is defined in terms of evidence a test can collect, and the attestation is a judgment that the actual result did or did not correspond.
epo:accountableOrganizationRole on the test-item access (the first party is the test item provider); sysml part def AccountableOrganization

Ruling R-21: the organization accountable for the test item, whose headword is now test item provider (sheet 08). ISO/IEC 17000 4.3 Note 1: the first-, second- and third-party descriptors are not the legal identification of the parties to a contract; the contract here is between the sponsor and the testing organization. Concern C-25 asks whether the three party terms stay three adopted headwords.

Evaluation performed by the organization that provides or is accountable for the test item: the test item provider. In OG-CAIE the test item provider is a party to every evaluation, since it grants access to the test item, but it does not perform the evaluation unless it is also the sponsor and the testing organization, and the record says so.
A requirement on the system stating what may be shared with a user and what must be withheld. Recommendations at the end of an evaluation typically propose changes to guardrails.
an RDF data graph conforming to the DSO
The body of domain facts, expressed in an ontology's vocabulary, that answers are judged against. It conforms to the ontology and may hold more context than the ontology alone.
epo:Report passRate carries an uncertainty when estimated from replicates; coverage does not

A non-negative number that says how dispersed the values attributed to a measured quantity are. A probe pass rate estimated from replicate sessions carries one; coverage, counted exactly over the record, does not.
sysml item def Mission, port def MissionWrite, seams missionSeam and missionToExecutiveSeam; epo:Mission with epo:regards the populations
Ruling R-37: a seam of its own from the sponsor, feeding the contract; the obligations towards the affected populations are the sponsor's mission and policy in ISO 9000's words, not a coinage.

The sponsor organization's purpose for existing, as its top management expresses it, and with it the obligations and duties it holds towards the affected populations. Recorded before the need is stated, it is the context the contract answers to: what the sponsor owes the people the test item will serve. Pinned at the contract.
narration in docs/contracting.md; no node of the record

Ruling R-36: the headword is ISO 9000's monitoring, the doctrine is ISO/IEC 17000's surveillance, kept as the alternative label with its clause so the concept stays mapped. Ruling R-35: narration in the Contracting chapter, outside the lifecycle.

Determining the status of a system at different stages or times. After an evaluation, a sponsor may require the test item provider to change the system per the findings and then require new testing to certify that the flagged issues were addressed; in conformity assessment that repeat is called surveillance. Observed in practice; not a step of the contracting lifecycle.

Ruling R-13: the sensitivity the authors describe, a small change of input producing a large change of output especially when a trajectory is continued, is stated here in prose; no term is coined for it.

A system that, given the same inputs and starting state, will not always produce the same outputs. The system under test is one, which is why a single probe is weak evidence and why pass rates are estimated over replicate sessions.
epo:Evidence (bears on one criterion, under a test plan) derived from epo:Response or epo:Trajectory
Rulings R-18 and R-20: evidence exists at probe, session or suite level and maps to an expected result; it is the domain, and the determination on it is the codomain.

Data that supports the existence or truth of something. Here, what is collected as the basis for a determination: a response at one turn, a session's trajectory, or several of them rolled up over a test suite, as in a robustness battery. Each evidence item bears on one acceptance criterion's expected result and is bound to the test plan it was collected under. Evidence is the domain; the determination made on it, passed, failed or cannot tell, is the codomain. On its own evidence verifies nothing; a determination rules on it and an attestation judges it.
sysml package OGCAIE; part def OgCaieEvaluation
Zargham and Hollek, for this specification (ruling R-47, sheet 06-10)

Contextual AI Evaluation performed with the method this specification sets out: the Evaluation Process Ontology, the same six steps for every domain inside a contracting lifecycle, applied with a Domain-Specific Ontology supplied or approved by the domain's experts, leaving a record anyone can check for conformance, traceability and coverage.
A shared, formal vocabulary for a domain, precise enough that a computer can check whether a body of data follows its rules.
epo:RequirementSet with epo:environment and epo:systemUnderTest; sysml item def RequirementSet

Rulings R-03 and R-14: a house label for the requirement set bound to one system under test in one operational environment; not a coinage. Two evaluations are comparable only when they share an envelope.

The requirements this system under test must meet in this operational environment, with their acceptance criteria and weights, declared before any probe is run. It refines the idea of a requirement by adding specificity: the same system in a different environment, or a different system in the same environment, gets a different envelope. That is what makes the evaluation contextual, and what separates it from a benchmark; the nearest practice is that of safety-critical systems. Coverage is measured over the envelope and only over it.
epo:RequirementSet declares it; sysml item def RequirementSet
The conditions and assumptions about the deployment setting under which acceptable behavior is defined: who uses the system, for what, and what is out of scope.

A person or group of people with its own functions, responsibilities and authorities. Three organizations are parties to every OG-CAIE evaluation: the sponsor organization that commissions it, the testing organization that performs it (the evaluation service provider), and the test item provider accountable for the AI system under test. Any two of them may be the same organization, and the record says whether they are.
earl:outcome with earl:passed, earl:failed, earl:cantTell, earl:inapplicable, earl:untested; sysml enum Outcome
Ruling R-47 (sheet 06-06): the canonical definition is SEVOCAB's test result; EARL supplies the binding, not the definition.
The result recorded for a judgment: passed, failed or cannot tell, the three EARL values the record uses (EARL also allows inapplicable and untested). Not binary on purpose.
A measurable result. Here: how the system did on what was exercised, reported as the pass, fail and cannot-tell fractions of the covered criteria. Never merged with coverage.
epo:Probe, a prov:Entity; sysml item def Probe

A scenario tied to the acceptance criteria it exercises, derived from the Domain-Specific Ontology and checked for consistency before use, applied at one turn of a session. Its run yields one prompt and response pair; the response collected is evidence bearing on those criteria. A test plan may list its probes or choose them by a test strategy as the trajectory unfolds.
epo:ProviderRole, the genus of epo:EvaluationServiceProviderRole and epo:TestItemProviderRole; sysml part def Organization

Ruling R-21 named the testing organization the provider; the tbox audit (sheet 08, on Z's instruction) keeps provider as ISO 9000's genus and makes its two specializations explicit as narrower terms: evaluation service provider (the testing organization) and test item provider (the accountable organization). ISO 9000:2026 3.1.9 Note 2 says a provider in a contractual situation is sometimes called a contractor, hence the altLabel.

An organization that provides a product or a service. Two products change hands around an OG-CAIE evaluation, so there are two providers: the evaluation service provider, the testing organization, provides the evaluation as a service; the test item provider provides, and is accountable for, the AI system under test. They are different organizations when the evaluation is independent, and the record states that fact rather than assuming it.
prov:Bundle; any prov:Entity of the record
Ruling R-48 (sheet 07-03): record is the abstract term and evaluation record its specialization, by subclassing; the narrower relation below says so.

A document stating results achieved or giving evidence of activities performed: any document that records what was done or what was found, in the most general sense the standard gives the word. The evaluation record is its special case here, the record of one evaluation; the DSO release, the test plan and the report are records too, each in its own right.
sysml part def EvaluationOperator (red teamer); epo:Session with a prov:Person in the evaluation operator role
A testing level in which human testers probe the system adversarially to see whether it stays within its guardrails. One way to run the probes in step four.
replicate epo:Session activities under one Strategy against one SUT version; minPassRate on the criterion

How closely results agree when the same measurement is repeated under the same conditions: same system version, same procedure, same operator or policy, same session protocol, over a short period. Replicate sessions under repeatability conditions are what turn a probe into a pass rate.
the record's fixed frame: requirement set, DSO release, test plan, session protocol

How closely results agree when the measurement is repeated under changed conditions: different operators, different sessions, a different evaluation team. Two evaluations that share a requirement set and a DSO release are comparable to the extent their results reproduce.
Something the system must do, or a condition it must meet, to be fit for its purpose. Broad requirements are decomposed into acceptance criteria that can be checked one at a time.
the chain requirement, acceptance criterion, test plan, probe, turn, evidence, attestation in the record; queries/traceback.rq

Ruling R-15: requirements traceability and metrological traceability are kept distinct, but they are in principle the same idea at different levels of abstraction once both are done computationally over knowledge graphs. Here computational instruments measure computational systems, so the metrological sense still applies: the chain from a reported number back to the record is an unbroken documented chain, and the pass rate it reaches carries a measurement uncertainty.
The documented path linking what was required to how it was tested and what was found, so a coverage claim can be checked by anyone holding the record.
Testing in which what is tested, and how much, is chosen according to analyzed risk. Deployment sensitivity is the weight that makes coverage reflect consequence.
A step-by-step description of a situation the system is put through: the user, their circumstances, and what they ask. A scenario becomes a probe once it is tied to the criteria it exercises.
epo:sponsorRole when the sponsor is not the test item provider (record fact epo:isAccountable, S0)

Evaluation performed by, or on behalf of, an organization with a user interest in the test item: a purchaser, a regulator, a deploying agency. A sponsor that is not the test item provider commissions the evaluation in this position.
epo:Session, a prov:Activity (the test execution); sysml item def Session

One pairing of one tester with one system under test, in which a sequence of turns is run. Sessions are stateful: what the system says at a later turn depends on everything said before, so evidence belongs to its session, not only to its probe.
sysml part defs SponsorOrganization, TestingOrganization, AccountableOrganization, AffectedPopulation and the actor parts within the testing organization; prov:Person, prov:Organization

A person or organization that can affect, be affected by, or believe itself affected by a decision or activity. The parties (the sponsor, the testing organization, the test item provider), the people who act for them, and the affected populations are the stakeholders named in this specification; customers and providers are kinds of interested party in the standard's own examples.
sysml item def StatementOfWork, port def StatementOfWorkWrite, seams statementOfWorkSeam and statementOfWorkToExecutiveSeam; epo:StatementOfWork with epo:decides engagement decisions

Ruling R-40: a boundary item between the contract and its fulfilment; the sponsor decides, per affected population, interview or representation; the record must show the decision and the evaluation must realize it.

The sponsor's decisions about the work to be performed under the contract; here, for each affected population, whether it is interviewed, with its stakeholder needs documented as input, or represented by the domain expert. A scope-of-work judgment: representation is the common case, interviews are reserved for underrepresented stakeholders or underdocumented needs because of the effort they cost. Decided with the agreement, pinned at the contract, consumed by the scope step, and traceable either way.
epo:sufficiency on Attestation; sysml enum Sufficiency; judgment rules in shape S6

Sheet 10-12 (R-50), in Z's words: sufficiency relates the evidence to the claim that a requirement is met or not: insufficient evidence implies cannot tell, sufficient evidence can give pass or fail. One failing response can suffice to show a criterion unmet in that instance; shape S6 holds the rule.

The expert judgment that the evidence gathered is enough to support the claim being made. A quantity judgment, distinct from appropriateness. A judgment with no evidence cannot record a pass or a fail.
sysml part defs DomainExpert and EvaluationOperator; prov:Person

Ruling R-10: the ISO entry is marked <audit>; here the team is an evaluation team, not an audit team, and both the domain expert and the evaluation operator are technical experts on it (R-23 names the second). Assessors of the assessment are out of scope (R-11).

A person who provides specific knowledge or expertise to the evaluation team. Two kinds sit on the team. The domain expert is expert in the Domain-Specific Ontology: they supply or approve its release, attest that it is appropriate for the case being evaluated (this system under test, these requirements, this operational environment), and may be consulted on interpreting evidence. The evaluation operator is expert in performing the tests the Evaluation Process Ontology specifies, conditioned on the DSO, and in assembling the evidence.
epo:Session with its epo:Turn activities (test execution; each turn's epo:Response is the actual result)

Finding out whether requirements for a specific intended use are met. A session, in which probes are run turn by turn against the system under test, is a test; the evidence its turns yield feeds the attestations.
Inputs, execution conditions and expected results developed for a particular objective. The abstract test; a probe is a test case tied to the criteria it exercises.

Ruling R-01: coverage relates requirements to the abstract tests that cover them. The acceptance criterion is the coverage item and the probe is the test case; the concrete applications of a probe during a case produce evidence, which is rolled up by attestation. Coverage counts criteria with an attested outcome; it does not count evidence.
How much of the declared acceptance criteria the evaluation actually reached, as a share weighted by deployment sensitivity. It says how much was evaluated, not how well the system did.
sysml part def TestItem; earl:TestSubject and prov:SoftwareAgent; epo:systemUnderTest on the requirement set

Ruling R-19: the only standard definition of the phrase system under test is a 1999 performance-measurement one (ISO/IEC 14756), so the headword is test item (29119-2), from the same family as test case, test plan and test strategy; the systems-engineering reading is system-of-interest (15288) and the AI-evaluation reading is NIST's application. The phrase system under test stays in prose and in the model as the alternative label.
The deployed AI system being evaluated, taken as a black box: only what it is given and what it produces are recorded. The prose calls it the system under test; the standard headword is test item.
epo:TestItemCustomerRole; epo:testItemCustomerRole on the sponsor when it deploys the test item; epo:affectedAs epo:asCustomer on an affected population

Tbox audit (sheet 08, on Z's instruction): the customer of the AI system under test, distinguished explicitly from the customer of the evaluation. The affected populations of ruling R-21 are its customers or are affected through them; the record says which (epo:affectedAs).

A person or organization that receives the AI system under test as a product or a service: its users, and the organization that deploys it. An affected population is a test item customer when it uses the system; other populations are affected indirectly, through other stakeholders' use. The sponsor is a test item customer when it is the deploying organization, and may commission the evaluation on behalf of the populations who are.
epo:TestItemProviderRole; epo:accountableOrganizationRole on the test-item access; sysml part def AccountableOrganization

Sheet 09 (block B4) and the tbox audit (sheet 08): the headword accountable organization becomes test item provider, kept as the alternative label; it specializes ISO 9000's provider, with ISO/IEC 17000's first party as the neighbour. Ruling R-48 (07-06) asked whether accountable organization was the right headword; ruling R-49 (block B2) records the renaming.

The organization that provides, and is accountable for, the AI system under test: its vendor or its operator. It is a party to every evaluation because it grants access to the test item, but it does not perform the evaluation unless it is also the sponsor and the testing organization, and the record says so. In ISO/IEC 17000's terms it is the first party.
epo:TestPlan, a prov:Entity; sysml item def TestPlan

The statement, made before any test runs, of what the evaluation will test and how: which acceptance criteria are its objectives, which probes are its means, and what each probe is expected to show. Derived from the requirement set and the Domain-Specific Ontology in step three; every attestation is bound to the plan that produced its evidence.
epo:Strategy, a prov:Plan; a TestPlan's means alongside listed probes

Ruling R-13: anchored to output feedback because the record only ever holds outputs; the memory operator with the DSO as model is the observer. Semantic state feedback is the authors' framing, kept as an alternative label.

The part of a test plan that decides which probe comes next from the trajectory so far, grounded in the Domain-Specific Ontology, rather than listing probes in advance. It closes a loop: the system's outputs feed back into the choice of the next input. A human red teamer following their own judgment is one such strategy; a written policy is another.
epo:TestSuite, a prov:Activity grouping epo:Session activities

A set of sessions run together, for example replicate sessions of one strategy, or the varied sessions of a sensitivity test or robustness battery. Evidence rolled up over a suite is evidence at the third level, above probe and session.
epo:independentOfAccountable on the testing organization (record fact, S0)

Evaluation performed by an organization independent of the provider of the test item and with no user interest in it, and not on behalf of anyone who has one. Independence of the testing organization from the test item provider is what makes an OG-CAIE result independent; the record states it as a fact about the parties rather than assuming it, and states separately whether the sponsor has a user interest.
epo:Trajectory, a prov:Entity generated by a Session; ordered epo:Turn activities
Ruling R-13: the IEC trajectory runs through the hidden state x; what the record holds is the input-output realization, which specializes it to what is observable.

The recorded sequence of prompt and response pairs of a session, in order. The system's internal state is never observed; the trajectory is the observable realization, and plays the role a time series of measurements plays in system identification. A small change early in a trajectory can change everything after it.

Confirming with objective evidence that the requirements for a specific intended use were fulfilled. Applied to the evaluation itself: was it aimed at the right problem and is the evidence enough. Both are human judgments, recorded in the attestation.
SHACL shapes S0-S9 over the record and M1-M5 over the model graph (machine); SCI requirements tagged machine

Confirming with objective evidence that specified requirements were fulfilled. Applied to the evaluation itself: did it exercise what it declared, and was its declared process followed. Both are mechanical checks over the record.
The Domain-Specific Ontology release is versioned and approved by a named domain expert before any probe is derived from it.
The service agreement, the operational environment, the test item and the requirement set are declared, in that order, before any session runs: this system in this environment under this contract.
Every requirement has at least one acceptance criterion derived from it; every criterion states its expected result and carries a positive weight.
A test plan states its objectives and its means; every probe belongs to a plan, derives from the DSO release and passes a consistency check before any session.
Every response comes from a numbered turn of a session against a versioned test item; every evidence item bears on one criterion's expected result under the plan.
machine for form; human for the judgment

Determinations rule on evidence with an EARL outcome; attestations aggregate a criterion's determinations, name their assertor, and judge appropriateness and sufficiency; the closure and chain rules hold.
Coverage is recomputable from a conformant record: a criterion counts as covered only with an attestation behind it.
Coverage and performance are reported together and never merged.
machine for the trace; human for the recommendation
Every recommendation traces to the attestations it rests on, their evidence, the DSO release and the EPO step.

The sponsor, the testing organization and the accountable organization are named; the sponsor's mission and obligations towards the affected populations are recorded before the need, and its statement of work decides, per population, interview or representation; the agreement is signed by the sponsor and the authorized representative; every affected population is spoken for by a named representative on the team, and interviewed where the statement of work decided so.

The wiring guarantees the end state, checked locally over kinds of parts and ports: every wire runs from an output port on a part to an input port on a part carrying one item kind; at every part every input is present once and every output goes somewhere; every item kind reaches the recorder; the seven contracting steps (C1 to C6 with fulfil between access and delivery) and the six evaluation steps form process DAGs that produce every item kind; a conformant record then yields traceability in both directions and coverage, and answers why.

The domain expert who approves the DSO, assesses appropriateness and attests is not the evaluation operator who administers tests and collects evidence, and neither is the authorized representative who signs the agreement; one authorized representative, one or more of each expert.

What the contract pins (the counterparties, the test item, the requirements' frame, the method) is recorded and closed before what the evaluation pins (the environment, the requirement set, the DSO release, the plan) is declared; the evaluation documents the first layer and cannot change it.

The assembly relates the sponsor to the affected populations by an obligation: a connection usage typed Obligation whose ends are the sponsor part and the affected part, a relation that carries no item (R-38). The mission regards one or more affected populations: the Mission item owns a reference part typed AffectedPopulation with lower bound one (R-37, R-38).
nodes.label: M1-Obligation

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:PartDefinition. The assembly owns a part typed AffectedPopulation with lower bound zero: populations are many and may be absent (R-21). The assembly owns exactly one part typed by each of SponsorOrganization, TestingOrganization and AccountableOrganization (R-21); a second sponsor part or a missing one fails (sheet 10).
nodes.label: M1-Parties

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:PartDefinition. At the part: every input port is present on exactly one wire (input wires are unique, R-25, R-26). At the part: every output port goes somewhere, on one wire or several, since what flows is information (R-25, R-26).
nodes.label: M2-Part

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:InterfaceUsage. A wire runs from an output port on a part to an input port on a part: the output end is a plain port owned by a part definition, the input end a conjugated one (R-26). The input port's type is the wire's consumer end type, conjugated: it receives the same item kind. The output port's type is the wire's supplier end type: what flows is one item kind. A wire comes from exactly one output port. A wire goes to exactly one input port.
nodes.label: M2-Wire

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:PortDefinition. Every item kind that crosses a seam reaches the recorder: the recorder owns a conjugated port of this type (R-17).
nodes.label: M3-RecordHub

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:ItemDefinition. Every item kind is an out parameter of some step of the process, or the process's own result: nothing in the record appears from nowhere.
nodes.label: M4-EveryItemProduced

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:ActionDefinition. One nested model (R-33): the contracting lifecycle's fulfil step is a black box typed by the evaluation process. The inner process conforms to the layer above: every input of the evaluation process is fed by a flow from a contracting step, and every output feeds one (R-33).
nodes.label: M4-Nesting

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:SuccessionAsUsage. The EPO is a process DAG (R-26): no step succeeds itself, directly or through other steps.
nodes.label: M4-ProcessDag

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:ActionDefinition. The evaluation owns exactly six steps; the contracting lifecycle owns six of its own plus the nested fulfil step (R-21, R-32, R-33). The steps succeed one another in the fixed order: scope, declareRequirements, plan, execute, determineAndAttest, report for the evaluation; need, propose, agree, access, fulfil, deliver, acceptDelivery for the contracting lifecycle.
nodes.label: M4-Steps

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:PartDefinition. The evaluation team allows one or more domain experts and one or more operators: lower bound one, upper bound unbounded (R-23). The sponsor organization holds exactly one signatory (SponsorSignatory), the named person who signs, approves the requirement set and accepts on its behalf (sheet 10-06, R-50). The testing organization holds exactly one authorized representative (AccountExecutive) (R-23).
nodes.label: M5-Cardinality

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:PortUsage. DSO, appropriateness assessment, plan approval, report approval and attestation are supplied only by the domain expert (R-10, R-21, R-49). Evidence is supplied only by the evaluation operator, and a person applies probes to the test item only as the evaluation operator (R-12, R-23). The service agreement is supplied only by the sponsor's signatory and the authorized representative (sheet 10-06); the authorized representative supplies nothing but the proposal, the countersigned agreement, its independence declaration (sheet 10-07) and the delivery, and never judges (R-23, R-24, R-32). Where the sponsor signs, the port is its signatory's (sheet 10-06): the acceptance, the requirement-set approval and the user-interest declaration are supplied only by SponsorSignatory, a Person, and the sponsor organization supplies none of them.
nodes.label: M5-PortsBelongToRoles

nodes.desc: Targets sysml:Package. The testing organization holds an authorized representative (AccountExecutive) and a team of at least one domain expert and one evaluation operator. The three actor categories are distinct part definitions of Person: DomainExpert, EvaluationOperator, AccountExecutive (R-10, R-23).
nodes.label: M5-Roles

nodes.desc: Targets epo:TestItemAccess. S0: access to the test item is granted by the test item provider, the accountable organization (ISO/IEC 17000 first party), for a period that ends after it starts. Access is granted under the service agreement (sheet 10-05). Access names the instrument outside this agreement under which the provider owes it (sheet 10-04). Access names the test item it is granted to. Access states its period: from when (sheet 10-04). Access states its period: until when (sheet 10-04).
nodes.label: S0-Access

nodes.desc: Targets prov:Bundle. S0 independence at the department or organization level (sheet 10-15): the determiner and the operator of the session behind the evidence, and the assessor and the author of the requirement set, act on behalf of different units (prov:actedOnBehalfOf); at the organization level the units are organizations. S0 independence at the person level (sheet 10-15): the person who assesses the appropriateness of the requirement set is not attributed on the requirement set. S0 independence at the person level (sheet 10-15): the person who determines on evidence is not the operator of the session that evidence came from, unless a second determination on the same evidence by another person exists.
nodes.label: S0-Independence

nodes.desc: Targets epo:ServiceAgreement. S0 two layers (R-32): every item of the record pinned at the contract is generated no later than the requirement set, and every item pinned within the evaluation no earlier than the agreement.
nodes.label: S0-Layers

nodes.desc: Targets prov:Entity. S0: every entity, activity and agent of a record is a member of exactly one record, a prov:Bundle, through ogc:inRecord (sheet 10-31): an item outside every record would escape the constraints anchored on it.
nodes.label: S0-Member

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Mission. S0: the mission is the sponsor organization's, the need is stated under it, and it is an item of the need step (the step is derived through the model graph, sheet 10-33). The mission names the affected populations it holds obligations towards (R-37).
nodes.label: S0-Mission

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Need. S0: the need is stated by the sponsor organization, and is an item of the need step (the step is derived through the model graph, sheet 10-33).
nodes.label: S0-Need

nodes.desc: Targets epo:ServiceAgreement. S0: exactly one organization of the record holds each of the sponsor (evaluation customer), testing (evaluation service provider) and accountable (test item provider) roles (R-21). S0: the agreement is an item of the agree step: its class realizes an item kind the model's agree step produces (the step is derived through the model graph, sheet 10-33). S0: the agreement is signed by the authorized representative, a named person acting on behalf of the testing organization, the evaluation service provider (R-23; sheet 09). S0: the agreement is signed by the sponsor's signatory, a named person acting on behalf of the sponsor organization, the evaluation customer (sheet 10-06). S0: the agreement precedes the requirement set: requirements are agreed under the contract, not before it (R-21). S0: the provider fact agrees with the roles (sheet 10-09): the organization that says it provides the test item holds the test item provider's role and the one that holds the role says so; a sponsor that says it does not provide it does not hold the role. S0: the sponsor's user interest is declared, not assumed (sheet 10-07): a user-interest declaration in the record, attributed to the sponsor's signatory and dated, says true or false. S0: the testing organization's independence is declared, not assumed (sheet 10-07): an independence declaration in the record, attributed to the authorized representative and dated, names the test item provider it is independent of; a testing organization that holds the test item provider's role declares no such independence. The agreement accepts the proposal (sheet 10-05).
nodes.label: S0-Parties

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Population. S0: every affected population is spoken for: a stakeholder representation attributed to the person who speaks for it (epo:representedBy); where the statement of work decided an interview, a stakeholder input attributed to the population exists, the representation used it, and the population names who engaged it (epo:responsibleParty) (R-21, R-40, R-49 series wiring; sheet 10-13). S0: who speaks for an affected population is a named person on the testing organization's team, any member (sheet 10-13); who engaged it is a person or an organization (sheet 08).
nodes.label: S0-Population

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Proposal. S0: the proposal is the authorized representative's answer to the need, follows it, and is an item of the propose step (the step is derived through the model graph, sheet 10-33).
nodes.label: S0-Proposal

nodes.desc: Targets prov:Bundle. The record carries a label. The record states the level at which independence between the roles is required: person, department or organization (sheet 10-15). The synthetic tag is a boolean (sheet 10-43).
nodes.label: S0-Record

nodes.desc: Targets prov:Person. S0: a person holds at most one of the person roles: domain expert, evaluation operator, authorized representative, sponsor signatory (sheet 10-13; the disjointness axioms are on the role classes and do not reach persons).
nodes.label: S0-Roles

nodes.desc: Targets epo:StatementOfWork. S0: the statement of work decides, for every affected population of the record, exactly once, interview or representation (R-40). S0: the statement of work is an item of the agree step (the step is derived through the model graph, sheet 10-33). S0: the statement of work is the sponsor's decision (R-40), dated no later than the agreement it is under (sheet 10-05). The statement of work is under the service agreement (sheet 10-05).
nodes.label: S0-StatementOfWork

nodes.desc: Targets epo:DsoRelease. S1 precondition (sheet 08, R-49): every affected population's representation is available before the DSO release is approved: the population's stakeholder representation was generated before the release's approval time (a population with no representation at all is S0's finding). S1: a probe derived from this DSO release was generated before the release was approved. S1: the DSO release is approved by a domain expert (R-21, R-23). A DSO release is approved by a named person.
nodes.label: S1-DsoRelease

nodes.desc: Targets epo:AcceptanceCriterion. A criterion is a statement (GtWR C7: verifiable). A criterion is dated (sheet 10-10). A criterion says why it carries its weight (sheet 10-10). A criterion states its expected result: the observable behavior a test can collect (R-12). Deployment sensitivity: weight greater than zero. Every acceptance criterion derives from a requirement.
nodes.label: S2-AcceptanceCriterion

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Requirement. S2 downward traceability (R-17): a requirement with no acceptance criterion derived from it cannot be covered and is not traceable. A requirement belongs to the requirement set.
nodes.label: S2-Requirement

nodes.desc: Targets epo:RequirementSet. S2: a domain expert has assessed the requirement set as appropriate for the populations and the environment (R-08, R-21). S2: a probe run started, or a probe was generated, before the requirement set was declared. S2: the sponsor approves the requirement set (sheet 10-01): an approval attributed to the sponsor's signatory, dated after the set was declared and before any session of the record started. S2: the system under test the envelope binds is the one an access grant of the record names (sheet 10-17). The envelope names the one system under test it binds (R-14): this system, in this environment, must meet these requirements. The operational environment is stated. The requirement set is agreed under the service agreement (R-21).
nodes.label: S2-RequirementSet

nodes.desc: Targets epo:PlanApproval. S3 order (sheet 10-19): the plan is approved before any session whose turns use the plan's probes starts. S3: a test plan is approved by a domain expert (R-21).
nodes.label: S3-PlanApproval

nodes.desc: Targets epo:PlanDeviation. S3: a plan deviation is the evaluation operator's, and is an item of the plan step or the report step (the step is derived through the model graph, sheet 10-33). A deviation names the criterion it concerns (sheet 10-16). A deviation names the plan it departs from (sheet 10-16). A deviation states its reason (sheet 10-16).
nodes.label: S3-PlanDeviation

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Probe. S3 order (sheet 10-19): the probe's passed consistency check ended before the first turn that used the probe started. S3: every probe is a means of some test plan, directly or through a strategy that generated it. S3: no passed automatic consistency check exists for this probe. A probe names at least one acceptance criterion it exercises.
nodes.label: S3-Probe

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Strategy. A strategy is grounded in a DSO release. A strategy states its policy: how the next probe is chosen from the trajectory so far (R-13).
nodes.label: S3-Strategy

nodes.desc: Targets epo:TestPlan. S3 completion (sheet 10-16): every acceptance criterion of the record the plan leaves out, and every objective of the plan without an attestation, has a plan deviation with its reason that deviates from this plan and concerns that criterion. S3: a test plan derives from the requirement set and a DSO release. S3: every probe a plan names as a means exercises at least one of the plan's objectives. A test plan states at least one objective, an acceptance criterion. A test plan states its means: probes, or a strategy that chooses them (R-13).
nodes.label: S3-TestPlan

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Session. S4 binding (sheet 10-17): the session's software agent is the system under test the record's requirement set binds, and every determination on evidence from this session names that agent as its subject. S4: a session has at least one turn. S4: a session must be associated with a named person in the evaluation operator role; administering tests is the operator's activity, not the domain expert's (R-10, R-23). S4: a session must be associated with a versioned software agent (the system under test).
nodes.label: S4-Session

nodes.desc: Targets epo:TestSuite. S4: a test suite groups at least one session.
nodes.label: S4-TestSuite

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Turn. A turn applies exactly one probe.
nodes.label: S4-Turn

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Evidence. S5 order (sheet 10-19): evidence is generated no earlier than the turn its response came from started. S5: evidence is collected by the evaluation operator (sheet 10-15, mirroring M5-PortsBelongToRoles: the evidence port is the operator's). S5: evidence must derive from at least one response or trajectory. S5: the plan an evidence item is bound to must have the criterion it bears on as an objective. An evidence item bears on exactly one criterion's expected result (R-18, R-20). Evidence derives from a response (probe level), a trajectory (session level) or several of them (suite level). Evidence is attributed to whoever collected it. Evidence is bound to the test plan it was collected under.
nodes.label: S5-Evidence

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Response. A response is generated by exactly one turn; a response from nowhere is not a record.
nodes.label: S5-Response

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Attestation. S6 chain rule (R-12, R-18, R-20): every determination an attestation aggregates tests the attested criterion, and every evidence item it rules on bears on that criterion under a plan that has it as an objective. S6 closure rule: an attestation with outcome passed or failed must aggregate at least one determination that rules on evidence; with none it can only say cantTell. S6 judgment rules (sheet 10-12): passed or failed requires sufficient evidence; insufficient evidence implies cannot tell; an inappropriate context allows only cannot tell or inapplicable. S6 no cherry-picking (sheet 10-14): an attestation uses every determination of the record on its criterion that ended before it, or names the determination it left out with epo:excludes and gives its epo:reason. S6 order (sheet 10-19): an attestation ends no earlier than every determination it aggregates. S6: an attestation is an item of the determine-and-attest step (the step is derived through the model graph, sheet 10-33). S6: the attesting person holds the domain expert role; the operator collects and determines, the authorized representative signs and delivers, only the domain expert attests (R-21, R-23). An attestation is made by one named person. Appropriateness of the declared context is judged (R-08).
nodes.label: S6-Attestation

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Determination. S6 no cherry-picking (sheet 10-14): a determination uses every evidence item of the record that bears on its criterion under the plan and was generated before it ended, or names the item it left out with epo:excludes and gives its epo:reason. S6 order (sheet 10-19): a determination ends no earlier than the evidence it rules on was generated. S6: a determination is made by a domain expert, an evaluation operator, or a versioned software agent; never by the authorized representative (R-21, R-23). S6: every evidence item a determination uses must bear on the criterion the determination tests. A determination rules on at least one evidence item. A determination's outcome is passed, failed or cantTell (EARL); not a Boolean.
nodes.label: S6-Determination

nodes.desc: Targets epo:ConformanceVerdict. S7: the conformance verdict is asserted by a versioned software agent and judges the record it belongs to: its subject is that record (sheet 10-41; walkthrough, R-49). The verdict names the coverage query by its sha256 digest (sheet 10-18). The verdict names the ontology it ran by its sha256 digest (sheet 10-18). The verdict names the shapes it ran by their sha256 digest (tool qualification, sheet 10-18).
nodes.label: S7-ConformanceVerdict

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Report. S7 (SCI-08, sheet 10-19): the stored pass, fail and cannot-tell rates equal the rates recomputed from the record's attestations over the covered criteria, as queries/coverage.rq computes them (a criterion counts once: failed if any attestation failed, else passed if any passed, else cannot tell). S7 draft and final (sheet 10-41, Z: conformance is a prerequisite for compiling the final report; a draft may carry flagged gaps): a draft report flags its gaps; a final report used a passed conformance verdict on its record that ended no later than the report was generated. S7: the outcome distribution must sum to one. S7: the report must be computed by an automatic activity of a versioned software agent. S7: the stored coverage equals the coverage recomputed from the record: the weighted share of acceptance criteria that carry at least one attestation with an outcome (walkthrough B5, R-48). A report says whether it is a draft or final (sheet 10-41).
nodes.label: S7-Report

nodes.desc: Targets epo:ReportApproval. S7: the final report's contents are approved by a domain expert, after a passed conformance verdict on the record: correct construction is not enough, and a draft is not approved (walkthrough, R-49; sheet 10-41).
nodes.label: S7-ReportApproval

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Delivery. S8 order (sheet 10-19): the delivery is made no earlier than the report approval it carries ended. S8: a delivery is made by the authorized representative to the sponsor and carries a final report (the record's delivered export, sheets 10-02, 10-41), its approval by a domain expert, and the recommendation (walkthrough, R-49). S8: the delivery is an item of the deliver step (the step is derived through the model graph, sheet 10-33). The delivery is made under the service agreement (sheet 10-05).
nodes.label: S8-Delivery

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Recommendation. S8 no cherry-picking (sheet 10-11): a recommendation derives from every attestation the record's coverage computation used, or names the attestation it left out with epo:excludes and gives its epo:reason. S8: a recommendation derives from at least one evidence item. S8: a recommendation is an item of the report step (the step is derived through the model graph, sheet 10-33). S8: a recommendation must derive from at least one attestation. S8: a recommendation must name the DSO release it rests on. S8: a recommendation must name the test plan its evidence was produced under. S8: every attestation a recommendation rests on must itself rest on evidence the recommendation can reach. S8: the domain expert's report approval owns the recommendation: it derives from a report approval (sheet 10-11). A recommendation is a named person's.
nodes.label: S8-Recommendation

nodes.desc: Targets epo:Acceptance. S9 (sheet 10-03): acceptance recognizes completion of the contract's obligations; a correctly constructed record is necessary and not sufficient for it. The accepted delivery carries a final report that used a passed verdict on the record, and that report's approval. S9: the acceptance is the sponsor's signatory's act on behalf of the sponsor, follows the delivery it accepts, and is an item of the accept step (the step is derived through the model graph, sheet 10-33).
nodes.label: S9-Acceptance

nodes.desc: “An (auxiliary) assumption is a background claim held fixed in deriving and testing a prediction. Because predictions normally follow from a hypothesis together with auxiliary assumptions and initial conditions, a failed prediction does not by logic alone identify which component is false.” Where: The sponsor's mission towards the affected populations, the service agreement with its statement of work, and the access to the test item: the counterparties, the object, the requirements' frame and the method, fixed before the evaluation begins. Checkable: Pinned at the contract and timestamped before the requirement set; the evaluation takes them as given, documents them, and cannot change them.
nodes.label: row 2: auxiliary assumption, first layer (pinne…

nodes.desc: “An auxiliary assumption of the second layer is a claim about the domain and the deployment setting, declared and approved before any test and held fixed while it runs.” Where: The requirement set declaring this test item in this environment, and the DSO release, both declared and approved before any session. Checkable: Declared and timestamped before testing; every attestation says whether that declared context was appropriate.
nodes.label: row 3: auxiliary assumption, second layer (pinn…

nodes.desc: “In practice, however, falsification also depends on auxiliary assumptions and methodological judgments.” Where: The appropriateness and sufficiency judgments on every attestation, and the trace from each recommendation back to the requirement it answers. Checkable: A failed prediction is attributed: the record says which named person judged the context inappropriate or the evidence insufficient, and why.
nodes.label: row 7: context

nodes.desc: “Evidence is an accepted result of observation or experiment.” Where: The response or trajectory collected as evidence bearing on one criterion; the determination is the accepted result: passed, failed or cannot tell. Checkable: Evidence derives from a recorded response at a recorded turn; a determination rules only on evidence that bears on the criterion it tests.
nodes.label: row 5: evidence

nodes.desc: “Falsifiability is the property of excluding at least one possible empirical outcome.” Where: The attestation's outcome for each criterion, and the report's coverage over all of them. Checkable: A failed outcome is a recorded falsifier; coverage is recomputed from the record, and a criterion with no attestation counts zero.
nodes.label: row 6: falsifiability

nodes.desc: “A hypothesis is a conjectural claim that can be subjected to empirical tests and potentially falsified. Its empirical content lies partly in what it rules out: the more possible outcomes it excludes, the greater the risk it takes.” Where: An acceptance criterion derived from a requirement, stating the expected result a test could observe. Checkable: The expected result is written down before testing, so a determination can rule it not met.
nodes.label: row 1: hypothesis

nodes.desc: “A prediction is an observable consequence that should occur if the hypothesis and relevant auxiliary assumptions are true. An observation that should not occur under those conditions is a potential falsifier.” Where: A probe applied at a turn of a session under the test plan, against the criterion's expected result. Checkable: The plan names its objectives and means before any session; every probe names the criteria it exercises.
nodes.label: row 4: prediction

nodes.desc: acceptance: the sponsor's acceptance of the delivery as performance of the agreement
nodes.label: Acceptance

nodes.desc: acceptance criterion
nodes.label: AcceptanceCriterion

nodes.desc: an actor category: held by a named person within the testing organization (R-10, R-23)
nodes.label: ActorRole

nodes.desc: how a population is affected by the test item
nodes.label: Affectedness

nodes.desc: appropriateness assessment: the domain expert's judgment that the requirement set is appropriate for the populations and the environment (R-08, R-21)
nodes.label: AppropriatenessAssessment

nodes.desc: AppropriatenessValue
nodes.label: AppropriatenessValue

nodes.desc: attestation
nodes.label: Attestation

nodes.desc: authorized representative: the testing organization's interface with its contractual counterparties (sheet 09; the term's IRI keeps its former local name account-executive)
nodes.label: AuthorizedRepresentativeRole

nodes.desc: conformance verdict: the checker's automatic assertion that the record is correctly constructed to the shapes, traceable in both directions and covered; its subject is the record, and it precedes the final report (walkthrough, R-49; sheet 10-41, R-50). Carries the digests of the shapes, the ontology and the coverage query it ran (sheet 10-18)
nodes.label: ConformanceVerdict

nodes.desc: automatic consistency check of a probe
nodes.label: ConsistencyCheck

nodes.desc: coverage computation
nodes.label: CoverageComputation

nodes.desc: customer (ISO 9000:2026 3.9.1): person or organization that receives a product or a service; the genus of the two customers below
nodes.label: CustomerRole

nodes.desc: delivery: the final report, its approval and the recommendation handed to the sponsor by the authorized representative under the agreement (R-24; sheets 10-02, 10-41): the report is the record's delivered export, the record itself is not delivered
nodes.label: Delivery

nodes.desc: determination (ISO 9000:2026 3.11.1; the paper's judgment): the ruling on one or more evidence items that a criterion's expected result was met, not met, or cannot be told (R-20); the codomain of evidence
nodes.label: Determination

nodes.desc: domain expert: expert in the Domain-Specific Ontology (an alternative label of technical expert, R-10)
nodes.label: DomainExpertRole

nodes.desc: DSO release
nodes.label: DsoRelease

nodes.desc: how an affected population is engaged
nodes.label: Engagement

nodes.desc: engagement decision: for one affected population, interview or representation (R-40)
nodes.label: EngagementDecision

nodes.desc: evaluation customer (the sponsor): receives the evaluation as a service, signs the agreement, decides the statement of work, accepts the delivery
nodes.label: EvaluationCustomerRole

nodes.desc: evaluation operator: expert in performing the tests the EPO specifies (R-23)
nodes.label: EvaluationOperatorRole

nodes.desc: evaluation service provider (the testing organization): provides the evaluation as a service; ISO/IEC 17000 third party when independent of the test item provider and without a user interest
nodes.label: EvaluationServiceProviderRole

nodes.desc: evidence: collected material (a response, a trajectory, or several) bearing on one criterion's expected result, under the test plan (R-18, R-20); the domain of a determination
nodes.label: Evidence

nodes.desc: independence declaration: the testing organization's dated statement, made by its authorized representative, that it is independent of the test item provider (ISO/IEC 17000 4.5, 5.4; sheet 10-07)
nodes.label: IndependenceDeclaration

nodes.desc: the level at which independence between the roles is required (sheet 10-15, R-50)
nodes.label: IndependenceLevel

nodes.desc: mission: the sponsor's purpose and its obligations towards the affected populations (ISO 9000:2026 3.4.11; R-37), the context the contract answers to
nodes.label: Mission

nodes.desc: need: the sponsor's stated mission problem and measures of success (ISO 9000:2026 requirement: need or expectation that is stated)
nodes.label: Need

nodes.desc: a party's role: held by an organization (R-21)
nodes.label: PartyRole

nodes.desc: plan approval: the domain expert's approval of a test plan (R-21)
nodes.label: PlanApproval

nodes.desc: plan deviation: a recorded departure from the test plan with its reason, for a criterion left unplanned or a plan objective left without an attestation; the operator's, dated (sheet 10-16, R-50)
nodes.label: PlanDeviation

nodes.desc: affected population: a population of persons affected by the test item (ISO 9000:2026 3.1.4 interested party), as its customers or indirectly through others' use of it; engaged by interview or by representation, with a responsible party for the engagement
nodes.label: Population

nodes.desc: probe
nodes.label: Probe

nodes.desc: probe derivation
nodes.label: ProbeDerivation

nodes.desc: proposal: the testing organization's response to the sponsor's need, offering the service
nodes.label: Proposal

nodes.desc: provider (ISO 9000:2026 3.1.9): organization that provides a product or a service; the genus of the two providers below
nodes.label: ProviderRole

nodes.desc: recommendation
nodes.label: Recommendation

nodes.desc: report: coverage and performance recomputed over the record; a draft may carry flagged gaps, a final report (epo:draft false) rests on a passed verdict on the record (sheet 10-41)
nodes.label: Report

nodes.desc: report approval: a domain expert's approval of the final report's contents after the machine verdict on the record (walkthrough, R-49; sheet 10-41); the approval owns the recommendation (sheet 10-11)
nodes.label: ReportApproval

nodes.desc: requirement
nodes.label: Requirement

nodes.desc: requirement set (operational envelope): the requirements one system under test must meet in one operational environment (R-14)
nodes.label: RequirementSet

nodes.desc: requirement-set approval: the sponsor's approval of the requirement set, made by its signatory, dated after the set and before any session (sheet 10-01, R-50)
nodes.label: RequirementSetApproval

nodes.desc: response: what the system under test produced at one turn (the actual result)
nodes.label: Response

nodes.desc: a role in one evaluation: a party's (an organization's) or an actor's (a person's within the testing organization)
nodes.label: Role

nodes.desc: service agreement: the contract (ISO 9000:2026 3.3.13) to perform OG-CAIE as a service, signed by the sponsor's signatory and the testing organization's authorized representative, each on behalf of their organization (R-21, R-23, R-50); accepts the proposal
nodes.label: ServiceAgreement

nodes.desc: session (NIST AI 700-2): one tester, one system under test, a sequence of turns; the test execution
nodes.label: Session

nodes.desc: sponsor signatory: a named person acting on behalf of the sponsor organization, who signs the agreement, declares the sponsor's user interest, approves the requirement set and accepts the delivery (sheet 10-06, R-50)
nodes.label: SponsorSignatoryRole
