nodes.desc: A specific, checkable condition a response must meet for a requirement to count as satisfied. The unit that coverage is measured over: each criterion either traces to an attested outcome or it does not.
nodes.label: acceptance criteria

nodes.desc: The person who signs the contract for the testing organization and delivers the report and the recommendation to the sponsor: the organization's interface with its contractual counterparties. The authorized representative is not responsible for the determinations in the report; those belong to the technical experts, and the representative makes no determination and no attestation. An abstract actor category, filled by exactly one named person in each evaluation.
nodes.label: authorized representative

nodes.desc: The expert judgment that the declared context (operational environment, requirement set and Domain-Specific Ontology) was the right frame for the judgment being made. Not whether the system passed, and not whether there was enough evidence.
nodes.label: appropriateness

nodes.desc: The recorded judgment of a named person that links one acceptance criterion to the evidence reviewed and records an outcome, together with the judgments of appropriateness of the declared context and sufficiency of the evidence.
nodes.label: attestation

nodes.desc: The knowledge graph, populated with the facts of the situation and conforming to the Domain-Specific Ontology, against which responses are judged.
nodes.label: authoritative reference

nodes.desc: The record is correctly constructed: it satisfies every rule the Evaluation Process Ontology's shapes state about how an evaluation must be recorded. A mechanical yes or no, produced by machine. If the record conforms, the process was followed, its data is shaped, its required fields are filled, and coverage can be computed. A special case of conformity: fulfilment of the record-keeping requirements.
nodes.label: conformance

nodes.desc: Fulfilment of a requirement, in the ISO sense: the system under test conforms to an acceptance criterion when its response fulfils it, as a named person attests. For the machine-checked shape of the record itself, see conformance.
nodes.label: conformity

nodes.desc: The evaluation of a deployed AI system against the needs of a specific domain and deployment context, judged by people who know that domain. The class of evaluation this specification is for; OG-CAIE is the way it is performed here.
nodes.label: Contextual AI Evaluation

nodes.desc: The binding agreement between the sponsor organization and the testing organization to perform OG-CAIE as a service. It is signed by the sponsor and by the testing organization's authorized representative, precedes the requirement set and follows the mission, the need and the proposal in the record.
nodes.label: contract

nodes.desc: A person or organization that receives a product or a service. Two products change hands around an OG-CAIE evaluation, so there are two customers: the evaluation customer, the sponsor, receives the evaluation as a service; the test item customer receives the AI system under test, as the sponsor sometimes does and as the affected populations do when they use it. The two may be the same organization, and the record says whether they are.
nodes.label: customer

nodes.desc: The weight each acceptance criterion carries, set by the consequence of the system getting it wrong in this deployment. Coverage is computed against these weights so it reflects consequence rather than count.
nodes.label: deployment sensitivity

nodes.desc: The ruling, made on one or more evidence items, that a criterion's expected result was met, was not met, or cannot be told. It is the ruling made on evidence, recorded with an EARL outcome of passed, failed or cannot tell, made by machine or by a named person, and it is what an attestation aggregates for a criterion.
nodes.label: determination

nodes.desc: The ordered prompts to, and responses by, the system under test within one session. Its recorded form is the trajectory.
nodes.label: dialogue

nodes.desc: The vocabulary and relations of the problem domain, imported from an existing ontology or supplied by domain experts, that equip one evaluation with the concepts it needs. A domain expert supplies or approves the release used. It changes when the domain changes.
nodes.label: Domain-Specific Ontology

nodes.desc: Systematically determining how far something meets its specified criteria. An OG-CAIE evaluation determines, for a declared requirement set, which criteria the system under test met, and reports coverage and performance separately.
nodes.label: evaluation

nodes.desc: The organization that receives the evaluation as a service: the sponsor. It states its mission and its need, agrees the requirement set with the testing organization under a contract, decides the statement of work, and receives and accepts the report and the recommendation. It may also be the test item customer, and it may commission the evaluation on behalf of affected populations who are, or who are affected by, the test item's customers.
nodes.label: evaluation customer

nodes.desc: The technical expert who operates the evaluation: declares the requirement set with the sponsor, writes the test plan, administers the probes to the test item, collects the responses and the evidence per the plan, and drafts the report and the recommendation. The operator makes determinations but does not attest; attestation belongs to the domain expert. An abstract actor category, filled by a named person in each evaluation.
nodes.label: evaluation operator

nodes.desc: The reusable, domain-independent description of how a rigorous evaluation is run: the standard operating procedure whose six steps, performed inside the contracting lifecycle, make a coverage claim checkable when followed. It assumes a Domain-Specific Ontology is in place and does not change across domains.
nodes.label: Evaluation Process Ontology

nodes.desc: The record of one evaluation, bound by the Evaluation Process Ontology: the DSO release, the requirement set, the test plan, the probes, the sessions and their trajectories, the evidence, the attestations, the report and the recommendations, with who did what and when. The EPO determines what must be present for requirements traceability in both directions and for coverage, and makes all three checkable by machine; a conformant record therefore provides both traceability directions and coverage.
nodes.label: evaluation record

nodes.desc: The organization that provides the evaluation as a service: the testing organization. Its authorized representative signs the contract and delivers the report, its evaluation team does the work, and its machines keep the record. When it is independent of the test item provider and has no user interest in the test item, its activity is third-party in ISO/IEC 17000's sense; the record states that independence as a fact.
nodes.label: evaluation service provider

nodes.desc: The evaluators within the testing organization who jointly perform one evaluation: at least one domain expert and at least one evaluation operator, each an evaluator in the SQuaRE sense, the person who performs an evaluation. What ISO 9000 calls an audit team is the same shape of thing for an audit; the word audit is kept out of the headword because readers hear legal bearing in it that neither standard intends.
nodes.label: evaluation team

nodes.desc: What the system under test should observably do if it meets an acceptance criterion under the probe's conditions. Stated on the criterion before testing, so the criterion is defined in terms of evidence a test can collect, and the attestation is a judgment that the actual result did or did not correspond.
nodes.label: expected results

nodes.desc: Evaluation performed by the organization that provides or is accountable for the test item: the test item provider. In OG-CAIE the test item provider is a party to every evaluation, since it grants access to the test item, but it does not perform the evaluation unless it is also the sponsor and the testing organization, and the record says so.
nodes.label: first-party conformity assessment activity

nodes.desc: A requirement on the system stating what may be shared with a user and what must be withheld. Recommendations at the end of an evaluation typically propose changes to guardrails.
nodes.label: guardrail

nodes.desc: The body of domain facts, expressed in an ontology's vocabulary, that answers are judged against. It conforms to the ontology and may hold more context than the ontology alone.
nodes.label: knowledge graph

nodes.desc: A non-negative number that says how dispersed the values attributed to a measured quantity are. A probe pass rate estimated from replicate sessions carries one; coverage, counted exactly over the record, does not.
nodes.label: measurement uncertainty

nodes.desc: The sponsor organization's purpose for existing, as its top management expresses it, and with it the obligations and duties it holds towards the affected populations. Recorded before the need is stated, it is the context the contract answers to: what the sponsor owes the people the test item will serve. Pinned at the contract.
nodes.label: mission

nodes.desc: Determining the status of a system at different stages or times. After an evaluation, a sponsor may require the test item provider to change the system per the findings and then require new testing to certify that the flagged issues were addressed; in conformity assessment that repeat is called surveillance. Observed in practice; not a step of the contracting lifecycle.
nodes.label: monitoring

nodes.desc: A system that, given the same inputs and starting state, will not always produce the same outputs. The system under test is one, which is why a single probe is weak evidence and why pass rates are estimated over replicate sessions.
nodes.label: non-deterministic system

nodes.desc: Data that supports the existence or truth of something. Here, what is collected as the basis for a determination: a response at one turn, a session's trajectory, or several of them rolled up over a test suite, as in a robustness battery. Each evidence item bears on one acceptance criterion's expected result and is bound to the test plan it was collected under. Evidence is the domain; the determination made on it, passed, failed or cannot tell, is the codomain. On its own evidence verifies nothing; a determination rules on it and an attestation judges it.
nodes.label: objective evidence

nodes.desc: Contextual AI Evaluation performed with the method this specification sets out: the Evaluation Process Ontology, the same six steps for every domain inside a contracting lifecycle, applied with a Domain-Specific Ontology supplied or approved by the domain's experts, leaving a record anyone can check for conformance, traceability and coverage.
nodes.label: OG-CAIE

nodes.desc: A shared, formal vocabulary for a domain, precise enough that a computer can check whether a body of data follows its rules.
nodes.label: ontology

nodes.desc: The requirements this system under test must meet in this operational environment, with their acceptance criteria and weights, declared before any probe is run. It refines the idea of a requirement by adding specificity: the same system in a different environment, or a different system in the same environment, gets a different envelope. That is what makes the evaluation contextual, and what separates it from a benchmark; the nearest practice is that of safety-critical systems. Coverage is measured over the envelope and only over it.
nodes.label: operational envelope

nodes.desc: The conditions and assumptions about the deployment setting under which acceptable behavior is defined: who uses the system, for what, and what is out of scope.
nodes.label: operational environment

nodes.desc: A person or group of people with its own functions, responsibilities and authorities. Three organizations are parties to every OG-CAIE evaluation: the sponsor organization that commissions it, the testing organization that performs it (the evaluation service provider), and the test item provider accountable for the AI system under test. Any two of them may be the same organization, and the record says whether they are.
nodes.label: organization

nodes.desc: The result recorded for a judgment: passed, failed or cannot tell, the three EARL values the record uses (EARL also allows inapplicable and untested). Not binary on purpose.
nodes.label: outcome

nodes.desc: A measurable result. Here: how the system did on what was exercised, reported as the pass, fail and cannot-tell fractions of the covered criteria. Never merged with coverage.
nodes.label: performance

nodes.desc: A scenario tied to the acceptance criteria it exercises, derived from the Domain-Specific Ontology and checked for consistency before use, applied at one turn of a session. Its run yields one prompt and response pair; the response collected is evidence bearing on those criteria. A test plan may list its probes or choose them by a test strategy as the trajectory unfolds.
nodes.label: probe

nodes.desc: An organization that provides a product or a service. Two products change hands around an OG-CAIE evaluation, so there are two providers: the evaluation service provider, the testing organization, provides the evaluation as a service; the test item provider provides, and is accountable for, the AI system under test. They are different organizations when the evaluation is independent, and the record states that fact rather than assuming it.
nodes.label: provider

nodes.desc: A document stating results achieved or giving evidence of activities performed: any document that records what was done or what was found, in the most general sense the standard gives the word. The evaluation record is its special case here, the record of one evaluation; the DSO release, the test plan and the report are records too, each in its own right.
nodes.label: record

nodes.desc: A testing level in which human testers probe the system adversarially to see whether it stays within its guardrails. One way to run the probes in step four.
nodes.label: red teaming

nodes.desc: How closely results agree when the same measurement is repeated under the same conditions: same system version, same procedure, same operator or policy, same session protocol, over a short period. Replicate sessions under repeatability conditions are what turn a probe into a pass rate.
nodes.label: repeatability

nodes.desc: How closely results agree when the measurement is repeated under changed conditions: different operators, different sessions, a different evaluation team. Two evaluations that share a requirement set and a DSO release are comparable to the extent their results reproduce.
nodes.label: reproducibility

nodes.desc: Something the system must do, or a condition it must meet, to be fit for its purpose. Broad requirements are decomposed into acceptance criteria that can be checked one at a time.
nodes.label: requirement

nodes.desc: The documented path linking what was required to how it was tested and what was found, so a coverage claim can be checked by anyone holding the record.
nodes.label: requirements traceability

nodes.desc: Testing in which what is tested, and how much, is chosen according to analyzed risk. Deployment sensitivity is the weight that makes coverage reflect consequence.
nodes.label: risk-based testing

nodes.desc: A step-by-step description of a situation the system is put through: the user, their circumstances, and what they ask. A scenario becomes a probe once it is tied to the criteria it exercises.
nodes.label: scenario

nodes.desc: Evaluation performed by, or on behalf of, an organization with a user interest in the test item: a purchaser, a regulator, a deploying agency. A sponsor that is not the test item provider commissions the evaluation in this position.
nodes.label: second-party conformity assessment activity

nodes.desc: One pairing of one tester with one system under test, in which a sequence of turns is run. Sessions are stateful: what the system says at a later turn depends on everything said before, so evidence belongs to its session, not only to its probe.
nodes.label: session

nodes.desc: A person or organization that can affect, be affected by, or believe itself affected by a decision or activity. The parties (the sponsor, the testing organization, the test item provider), the people who act for them, and the affected populations are the stakeholders named in this specification; customers and providers are kinds of interested party in the standard's own examples.
nodes.label: stakeholder

nodes.desc: The sponsor's decisions about the work to be performed under the contract; here, for each affected population, whether it is interviewed, with its stakeholder needs documented as input, or represented by the domain expert. A scope-of-work judgment: representation is the common case, interviews are reserved for underrepresented stakeholders or underdocumented needs because of the effort they cost. Decided with the agreement, pinned at the contract, consumed by the scope step, and traceable either way.
nodes.label: statement of work

nodes.desc: The expert judgment that the evidence gathered is enough to support the claim being made. A quantity judgment, distinct from appropriateness. A judgment with no evidence cannot record a pass or a fail.
nodes.label: sufficiency

nodes.desc: A person who provides specific knowledge or expertise to the evaluation team. Two kinds sit on the team. The domain expert is expert in the Domain-Specific Ontology: they supply or approve its release, attest that it is appropriate for the case being evaluated (this system under test, these requirements, this operational environment), and may be consulted on interpreting evidence. The evaluation operator is expert in performing the tests the Evaluation Process Ontology specifies, conditioned on the DSO, and in assembling the evidence.
nodes.label: technical expert

nodes.desc: Finding out whether requirements for a specific intended use are met. A session, in which probes are run turn by turn against the system under test, is a test; the evidence its turns yield feeds the attestations.
nodes.label: test

nodes.desc: Inputs, execution conditions and expected results developed for a particular objective. The abstract test; a probe is a test case tied to the criteria it exercises.
nodes.label: test case

nodes.desc: How much of the declared acceptance criteria the evaluation actually reached, as a share weighted by deployment sensitivity. It says how much was evaluated, not how well the system did.
nodes.label: test coverage

nodes.desc: The deployed AI system being evaluated, taken as a black box: only what it is given and what it produces are recorded. The prose calls it the system under test; the standard headword is test item.
nodes.label: test item

nodes.desc: A person or organization that receives the AI system under test as a product or a service: its users, and the organization that deploys it. An affected population is a test item customer when it uses the system; other populations are affected indirectly, through other stakeholders' use. The sponsor is a test item customer when it is the deploying organization, and may commission the evaluation on behalf of the populations who are.
nodes.label: test item customer

nodes.desc: The organization that provides, and is accountable for, the AI system under test: its vendor or its operator. It is a party to every evaluation because it grants access to the test item, but it does not perform the evaluation unless it is also the sponsor and the testing organization, and the record says so. In ISO/IEC 17000's terms it is the first party.
nodes.label: test item provider

nodes.desc: The statement, made before any test runs, of what the evaluation will test and how: which acceptance criteria are its objectives, which probes are its means, and what each probe is expected to show. Derived from the requirement set and the Domain-Specific Ontology in step three; every attestation is bound to the plan that produced its evidence.
nodes.label: test plan

nodes.desc: The part of a test plan that decides which probe comes next from the trajectory so far, grounded in the Domain-Specific Ontology, rather than listing probes in advance. It closes a loop: the system's outputs feed back into the choice of the next input. A human red teamer following their own judgment is one such strategy; a written policy is another.
nodes.label: test strategy

nodes.desc: A set of sessions run together, for example replicate sessions of one strategy, or the varied sessions of a sensitivity test or robustness battery. Evidence rolled up over a suite is evidence at the third level, above probe and session.
nodes.label: test suite

nodes.desc: Evaluation performed by an organization independent of the provider of the test item and with no user interest in it, and not on behalf of anyone who has one. Independence of the testing organization from the test item provider is what makes an OG-CAIE result independent; the record states it as a fact about the parties rather than assuming it, and states separately whether the sponsor has a user interest.
nodes.label: third-party conformity assessment activity

nodes.desc: The recorded sequence of prompt and response pairs of a session, in order. The system's internal state is never observed; the trajectory is the observable realization, and plays the role a time series of measurements plays in system identification. A small change early in a trajectory can change everything after it.
nodes.label: trajectory

nodes.desc: Confirming with objective evidence that the requirements for a specific intended use were fulfilled. Applied to the evaluation itself: was it aimed at the right problem and is the evidence enough. Both are human judgments, recorded in the attestation.
nodes.label: validation

nodes.desc: Confirming with objective evidence that specified requirements were fulfilled. Applied to the evaluation itself: did it exercise what it declared, and was its declared process followed. Both are mechanical checks over the record.
nodes.label: verification

nodes.desc: DsoApprovedBeforeProbes: The Domain-Specific Ontology release is versioned and approved by a named domain expert before any probe is derived from it. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-01

nodes.desc: EnvelopeDeclaredBeforeSessions: The service agreement, the operational environment, the test item and the requirement set are declared, in that order, before any session runs: this system in this environment under this contract. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-02

nodes.desc: CriteriaWellFormed: Every requirement has at least one acceptance criterion derived from it; every criterion states its expected result and carries a positive weight. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-03

nodes.desc: PlanBeforeRuns: A test plan states its objectives and its means; every probe belongs to a plan, derives from the DSO release and passes a consistency check before any session. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-04

nodes.desc: EvidenceFromNamedRuns: Every response comes from a numbered turn of a session against a versioned test item; every evidence item bears on one criterion's expected result under the plan. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-05

nodes.desc: AttestationsWellFormed: Determinations rule on evidence with an EARL outcome; attestations aggregate a criterion's determinations, name their assertor, and judge appropriateness and sufficiency; the closure and chain rules hold. [machine for form; human for the judgment]
nodes.label: SCI-06

nodes.desc: CoverageRecomputable: Coverage is recomputable from a conformant record: a criterion counts as covered only with an attestation behind it. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-07

nodes.desc: CoverageAndPerformanceKeptApart: Coverage and performance are reported together and never merged. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-08

nodes.desc: RecommendationTraceable: Every recommendation traces to the attestations it rests on, their evidence, the DSO release and the EPO step. [machine for the trace; human for the recommendation]
nodes.label: SCI-09

nodes.desc: PartiesNamedAndAgreed: The sponsor, the testing organization and the accountable organization are named; the sponsor's mission and obligations towards the affected populations are recorded before the need, and its statement of work decides, per population, interview or representation; the agreement is signed by the sponsor and the authorized representative; every affected population is spoken for by a named representative on the team, and interviewed where the statement of work decided so. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-10

nodes.desc: EndStateGuaranteed: The wiring guarantees the end state, checked locally over kinds of parts and ports: every wire runs from an output port on a part to an input port on a part carrying one item kind; at every part every input is present once and every output goes somewhere; every item kind reaches the recorder; the seven contracting steps (C1 to C6 with fulfil between access and delivery) and the six evaluation steps form process DAGs that produce every item kind; a conformant record then yields traceability in both directions and coverage, and answers why. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-11

nodes.desc: RolesDistinct: The domain expert who approves the DSO, assesses appropriateness and attests is not the evaluation operator who administers tests and collects evidence, and neither is the authorized representative who signs the agreement; one authorized representative, one or more of each expert. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-12

nodes.desc: TwoLayersOfAssumptions: What the contract pins (the counterparties, the test item, the requirements' frame, the method) is recorded and closed before what the evaluation pins (the environment, the requirement set, the DSO release, the plan) is declared; the evaluation documents the first layer and cannot change it. [machine]
nodes.label: SCI-13

nodes.desc:
The sponsor's act on receipt of the deliverables, recognizing
 completion of the contract's obligations (ISO/IEC/IEEE 24748-5
 acceptance): the signatory's act on behalf of the sponsor. A
 correctly constructed record is necessary and not sufficient for
 it (sheet 10-03, R-50). Pinned at the contract.
nodes.label: Acceptance

nodes.desc:
Derived from a requirement; states its expected result
 (SEVOCAB) and its weight, the deployment sensitivity (R-05,
 which specializes risk-based testing). The coverage item (R-01).
nodes.label: AcceptanceCriterion

nodes.desc:
Signatory of the service agreement and legal representative
 of the testing organization (ruling R-23; headword authorized
 representative, R-49). Countersigns the agreement into the
 record, reads the record through its view, and delivers the
 report and the recommendation to the sponsor as one delivery
 (an activity of its own, R-24); answers the sponsor's need with
 the proposal and receives the acceptance (R-32). No evidence, determination or
 attestation port: the authorized representative is not
 responsible for the determinations in the report; it is the
 organization's interface with its contractual counterparties
 (sheet 09), and declares its independence of the test item
 provider (sheet 10-07). The worked example's Mala.
nodes.label: AccountExecutive

nodes.desc: in port typed AcceptanceWrite, carrying Acceptance.
nodes.label: AccountExecutive::acceptanceIn

nodes.desc: in port typed AgreementWrite, carrying ServiceAgreement.
nodes.label: AccountExecutive::agreementIn

nodes.label: AccountExecutive::agreementOut

nodes.label: AccountExecutive::deliveryOut

nodes.label: AccountExecutive::independenceDeclarationOut

nodes.desc: in port typed StatementOfWorkWrite, carrying StatementOfWork.
nodes.label: AccountExecutive::statementOfWorkIn

nodes.desc:
The organization that provides or is accountable for the
 test item: the first party in ISO/IEC 17000's sense (4.3). It
 grants access to the test item and is named in the record.
nodes.label: AccountableOrganization

nodes.desc: out port typed AccessWrite, carrying TestItemAccess.
nodes.label: AccountableOrganization::accessOut

nodes.desc: OGCAIE::AccountableOrganization::testItem
nodes.label: AccountableOrganization::testItem : TestItem

nodes.desc:
A population of actors affected by the test item (ISO
 9000:2026 3.1.4 interested party, ruling R-21): always spoken for
 by a representative on the team, and interviewed where the
 statement of work decided so, in which case its input feeds the
 representation and enters the record (series wiring, R-49).
nodes.label: AffectedPopulation

nodes.desc: out port typed StakeholderInputWrite, carrying StakeholderInput.
nodes.label: AffectedPopulation::inputOut

nodes.desc:
The domain expert's assessment that the requirement set is
 appropriate for the affected populations and the environment
 (R-08, R-21).
nodes.label: AppropriatenessAssessment

nodes.desc:
ISO/IEC 17000 7.3: a named domain expert's statement for one
 criterion, aggregating its determinations, with outcome,
 appropriateness and sufficiency (R-08, R-20, R-21).
nodes.label: Attestation

nodes.desc:
Machine verification, called conformance (ruling R-16): the
 record is correctly constructed to the EPO shapes, traceable in
 both directions and covered; its verdict on the record is
 recorded and read by the assembler (walkthrough, R-49; sheet
 10-41, R-50). One output, read by two (R-25).
nodes.label: ConformanceChecker

nodes.desc: in port typed RecordWrite, carrying EvaluationRecord.
nodes.label: ConformanceChecker::recordIn

nodes.desc: out port typed ConformanceVerdictWrite, carrying ConformanceVerdict.
nodes.label: ConformanceChecker::verdictOut

nodes.desc:
The conformance checker's verdict on the record: correctly
 constructed to the shapes, traceable in both directions and
 covered (walkthrough, R-49; sheet 10-41, R-50). Conformance is a
 prerequisite for compiling the final report. Pinned within the
 evaluation.
nodes.label: ConformanceVerdict

nodes.desc:
The contracting lifecycle: the ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 agreement
 processes as SEBoK describes them, ISO/IEC 17000's access,
 scheme and acceptance, ISO 9000's contract (ruling R-32). One
 nested model (ruling R-33): the fulfil step is a black box typed
 by the EvaluationProcess, whose inputs are what the contract
 pinned and whose outputs are what the delivery carries; its
 definition below is the drill-down, and it conforms to that
 interface by typing. The flows say which item goes where.
nodes.label: ContractingProcess

nodes.label: ContractingProcess::acceptDelivery

nodes.label: ContractingProcess::access

nodes.desc:
The report and the recommendation handed to the sponsor by
 the account executive: the output of the delivery activity,
 distinct from recommending (ruling R-24).
nodes.label: Delivery

nodes.desc:
The ruling on evidence: passed, failed or cantTell; the
 codomain (ISO 9000:2026 3.11.1; R-20).
nodes.label: Determination

nodes.desc:
The technical expert (ISO 9000:2026 3.12.9) in the domain
 (rulings R-10, R-21): supplies or approves the DSO release,
 assesses the appropriateness of the requirement set for the
 affected populations, approves test plans, may make
 determinations on evidence (an activity either expert may
 perform, R-24), and attests. Represents the
 populations that are not interviewed. The worked example's
 Annie.
nodes.label: DomainExpert

nodes.desc: out port typed AssessmentWrite, carrying AppropriatenessAssessment.

nodes.desc:
A versioned release of the Domain-Specific Ontology,
 approved by a named domain expert before any probe is derived.
nodes.label: DsoRelease

nodes.desc:
The technical expert who operates the evaluation (SEVOCAB
 operator, refined; rulings R-10, R-23): declares the
 requirement set, writes the test plan, applies the probes to
 the test item, collects the evidence, makes determinations,
 records the deviations from the plan, and writes the
 recommendation. Responsible for the human roles in the test plan,
 the test driver for the machine work (sheet 10-20). No
 attestation port: attestation belongs to the domain expert. The
 worked example's Theo.

The Evaluation Process Ontology. Domain-independent; the
 agreement and the access enter from the contracting lifecycle;
 the DSO enters as a parameter at the scope step; the record
 leaves as the result.

The report step opened (sheet 10-41, R-50): the checker
 judges the record and its verdict precedes the report; the
 assembler reads the record and the verdict; a final report
 rests on a passed verdict, and the approval and the delivery
 take the final report only.
nodes.label: EvaluationProcess::report

nodes.desc: OGCAIE::EvaluationProcess::scope
nodes.label: EvaluationProcess::scope

nodes.desc:
The record itself (ISO 9000:2026 3.8.12, refined): a bundle
 (prov:Bundle) every item and agent is a member of, the hub every
 fact passes through, read by every machine and every member of
 the testing organization; auditable and reproducible, not
 delivered except as a special case (sheets 10-02, 10-31).
nodes.label: EvaluationRecord

nodes.desc:
The evaluation team (refined from ISO 9000:2026 3.12.7 audit
 team): at least one domain expert and at least one evaluation
 operator, distinct actor categories (rulings R-10, R-23).

Collected material bearing on one criterion's expected
 result under the plan; the domain (R-18, R-20).

The testing organization's declaration, made by its authorized
 representative and dated, that it is independent of the test item
 provider (ISO/IEC 17000 4.5, 5.4). Replaces a bare boolean on the
 organization (sheet 10-07, R-50). Pinned at the contract.

Versioned software (prov:SoftwareAgent). It derives, checks,

nodes.label: Person

nodes.desc:
A recorded departure from the plan, with its reason: a

 plan step or the report step. Pinned within the evaluation.

nodes.label: Probe

nodes.label: Recommendation

 one record port out, read by the three machines (output wires
 are shared when what flows is information, R-25); people read
 the record through their role's view (R-49).

nodes.desc:
Coverage and performance, computed by machine over the record
 and reported together, never merged: the record's delivered
 export (sheet 10-02). A draft may carry flagged gaps in
 traceability or coverage; a final report rests on a passed
 verdict on the record (sheet 10-41, R-50).
nodes.label: Report

nodes.desc:
A domain expert's approval of the final report's contents
 after the machine verdict: correct construction is not enough
 (walkthrough, R-49). Pinned within the evaluation.
nodes.label: ReportApproval

nodes.desc:
Assembles the report from the record and the verdict on it,
 coverage and the outcome distribution recomputed inside it;
 anyone holding the record recomputes the same numbers
 (queries/coverage.rq). A draft may carry flagged gaps; a final
 report rests on a passed verdict and is then approved by a domain
 expert (walkthrough, R-49; sheet 10-41, R-50).

nodes.label: ReportAssembler::recordIn

nodes.label: ReportAssembler::reportOut

 of work decided: every named population has one; any team member
 may be one, since speaking for a population is not a judgment on
 the test item (sheet 10-13); the population's interview, when it
 had one, feeds the representation (walkthrough B3, R-49).

nodes.label: Representative::inputIn

nodes.desc: out port typed RepresentationWrite, carrying StakeholderRepresentation.

nodes.desc:
The operational envelope (rulings R-03, R-14): the
 requirements THIS test item must meet in THIS operational
 environment, agreed under the service agreement.
nodes.label: RequirementSet

nodes.desc:
The sponsor's approval of the requirement set, made by its
 signatory, dated after the set and before any session (sheet
 10-01, R-50): the sponsor sees and approves what its test item is
 held to. Pinned within the evaluation.
nodes.label: RequirementSetApproval

nodes.desc: What the test item produced at one turn of a session.
nodes.label: Response

nodes.desc:
The contract (ISO 9000:2026 3.3.13) between the sponsor
 organization and the testing organization to perform OG-CAIE
 as a service, signed by the sponsor's signatory and by the testing
 organization's authorized representative, each acting on behalf
 of their organization (rulings R-21, R-23, R-50). It accepts the
 proposal; the statement of work, the access and the delivery are
 under it (sheet 10-05).
nodes.label: ServiceAgreement

nodes.desc:
One operator paired with the test item; its ordered turns
 form a trajectory (NIST AI 700-2; IEC 60050-351; R-13).
nodes.label: Session

nodes.desc:
The customer (ISO 9000:2026 3.9.1): states its mission and
 obligations towards the affected populations (R-37), states the need,
 receives the proposal, commissions the evaluation under the
 service agreement, receives the delivery through the authorized
 representative (R-32). Where a person signs, the port is the
 signatory's (sheet 10-06, R-50): the agreement, the acceptance,
 the requirement-set approval and the user-interest declaration.
 Whether it is also the test item provider, and whether it has a
 user interest in the test item, the record says by declaration.
nodes.label: SponsorOrganization

nodes.desc: in port typed DeliveryWrite, carrying Delivery.
nodes.label: SponsorOrganization::deliveryIn

nodes.desc: out port typed MissionWrite, carrying Mission.
nodes.label: SponsorOrganization::missionOut

nodes.desc:
The sponsor's signatory: a named person acting on behalf of the
 sponsor organization, the acquirer's authorized representative in
 SEVOCAB's acceptance (sheet 10-06, R-50). Signs the agreement,
 declares the sponsor's user interest, approves the requirement
 set, and accepts the delivery. The worked example's county health
 officer.
nodes.label: SponsorSignatory

nodes.desc: out port typed AcceptanceWrite, carrying Acceptance.
nodes.label: SponsorSignatory::acceptanceOut

 populations not interviewed are represented by the domain
 expert, and the record names who represents them (R-21).
nodes.label: StakeholderInput

nodes.desc:
What a representative says on behalf of an affected
 population, built from its interview when there was one:
 representation is always present for a named population, the
 interview layer is optional and feeds it (walkthrough B3, R-49).
 Pinned within the evaluation.
nodes.label: StakeholderRepresentation

nodes.desc:
The sponsor's scope-of-work decisions under the contract (SEVOCAB
 statement of work): for each affected population, interview or
 representation. A boundary item between the contract and its
 fulfilment (ruling R-40): decided with the agreement, consumed by
 the scope step. Pinned at the contract.
nodes.label: StatementOfWork

nodes.desc: OGCAIE::StatementOfWork::regards
nodes.label: StatementOfWork::regards : AffectedPopulation

nodes.desc:
A test strategy: a state feedback policy choosing the next
 probe from the trajectory so far (R-13). Optional.
nodes.label: Strategy

nodes.desc:
The machine part of administering the test plan (SEVOCAB test
 driver, walkthrough B8, R-49): derives the probes from the DSO
 release and the requirement set in the record; one output read
 by the operator and the recorder (an output wire may be shared,
 R-25).
nodes.label: TestDriver

nodes.desc: out port typed ProbeWrite, carrying Probe.
nodes.label: TestDriver::probesOut

nodes.desc: in port typed RecordWrite, carrying EvaluationRecord.
nodes.label: TestDriver::recordIn

nodes.desc:
The test item (SEVOCAB; the prose says system under test,
 ruling R-19): a black box that is given probes and produces
 responses. Provided by the accountable organization, inside
 the record, outside the testing organization's responsibility.
nodes.label: TestItem

nodes.desc:
The test item provider's grant of access to the test item under
 the agreement: the version identity, the access period, the
 instrument outside this agreement under which the provider owes
 the access, and the environment (sheet 10-04, R-50).
nodes.label: TestItemAccess

nodes.desc: in port typed ProbeWrite, carrying Probe.
nodes.label: TestItem::probesIn

nodes.desc: out port typed ResponseWrite, carrying Response.
nodes.label: TestItem::responseOut

nodes.desc:
SEVOCAB test plan: objectives (criteria) and means (probes
 or a test strategy), fixed before any session (R-12, R-13).
nodes.label: TestPlan

nodes.desc:
The provider (ISO 9000:2026 3.1.9): performs the evaluation
 as a service. Holds exactly one authorized representative, one
 team of one or more domain experts and one or more operators (all
 three are roles within it, ruling R-23), and the four machines.
 Independent of the test item provider, with no user interest in
 the test item, its activity is third-party (ISO/IEC 17000 4.5);
 its independence declaration in the record says so (sheet
 10-07).
nodes.label: TestingOrganization

 4.4, 4.5). Replaces a bare boolean on the organization (sheet
 10-07, R-50). Pinned at the contract.
nodes.label: UserInterestDeclaration

views.focus: every glossary term, the source it cites and the citation that carries the verbatim quote, canonical or neighbour.
views.label: Vocabulary
views.leaves_out: the rulings that settled a term, the essentials stated in it, and the model that binds it.

views.focus: every concern, the ruling that resolved it, and the terms a concern names or a ruling derives.
views.label: Rulings
views.leaves_out: the sources, the citations and the record; a ruling's words are in the panel, not on the canvas.

views.focus: the two cycles as the standards' steps, the item kinds each step consumes and produces, and the layer at which each kind is pinned.
views.label: Process
views.leaves_out: who performs a step and over which wire; the parts and the ports are in the wiring view.

views.focus: the parts of the assemblage, their ports, the seams that join an output port to an input port with the item kind that flows, and the one relation that carries no item.
views.label: Wiring
views.leaves_out: the steps and their order; the record; the vocabulary the part names come from.

views.focus: the measles evaluation: every recorded item, the agent that produced, signed or attested it, and the provenance chain between them.
views.label: Record
views.leaves_out: the step and the kind each item instantiates, one click away in the panel; the vocabulary and the rulings.

views.focus: the thirteen essentials, the shapes that check each (M over the model graph, S over the record), and the terms each is stated in.
views.label: Essentials
views.leaves_out: what each essential rests on, sources and rulings, and the record the S-shapes run over.

views.focus: the front page's bridge as data: each row of the crosswalk, the terms it lands on, the kinds and shapes that realize it, and the session it cites.
views.label: Crosswalk
views.leaves_out: everything on the far side of the bridge a row does not name; a row's own words are in the panel.

views.focus: every node and every link the explorer holds, as one graph.
views.label: Everything
views.leaves_out: legibility; use it to see the shape of the whole and a view to read a part.
